transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-04-14
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jared (Redwood SE), Priya (CSM), Liam (CedarBank Infosec), Sofia (CedarBank Platform), Rajiv (CedarBank App Sec)
Artifacts referenced: security deck (https://redwood.app/drive/security-deck), SOC2 report placeholder, Okta config doc link (shared after call)

00:00 - Maya: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, we'll run for ~40 minutes today, quick recap of last week and then deep dive into SSO and logs.  Priya is on for timing and next steps.
00:22 - Liam: Great, thanks. We spun up the staging connector, saw some logs, had a couple questions about retention and what exact fields are persisted.
00:35 - Jared: Yep, quick note — by default we persist full request/response token metadata for the pilot, but you can opt out per-route. So if there are PII-sensitive endpoints you can mark them and we'll redact or not persist.
01:10 - Rajiv: When you say "redact", is that at ingest or post-process? We need to ensure it never lands in plaintext logs.
01:25 - Jared: Good call. For the POC we can do ingest-time redaction via a route-level config. The pipeline supports tokenization and field-level redaction before writing to audit logs. I'll show the config in a follow-up doc.
02:02 - Sofia: And encryption at rest, KMS — you mentioned earlier we can use a customer-managed key?
02:12 - Maya: Yes — Redwood Private can integrate with your KMS/HSM; for Hosted we offer envelope encryption and we have a customer-managed KMS option for Dedicated. For the pilot, we can demo CMK usage in staging.
02:45 - Liam: OK, for compliance we need to see SOC 2 Type II and a summary of the pen test. Can you share that?
02:55 - Maya: Absolutely, I'll upload the SOC 2 packet and the last pen test summary to the shared drive after this call.
03:10 - Priya: We're going to also include a short FAQ for your security reviewers so they know where to find network controls, PCI/PII notes, and our retention defaults.
03:30 - Liam: That helps. What's your default retention for audit logs? 90 days? 1 year? It's important depending on our data retention policy.
03:42 - Jared: Default in Hosted is 90 days for verbose traces, 365 days for summary metrics. But routes and environments can override that — for Private you can configure indefinite retention depending on storage.
04:15 - Rajiv: If we need a 7-year archive for legal reasons, can you export logs to our S3 with server-side encryption?
04:25 - Maya: Yes — we support log export to customer S3 with SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS. For the POC we can set up a nightly export.
04:40 - Sofia: Is the export real-time or batched? We need near real-time for our monitoring tooling.
04:48 - Jared: Exports are batched nightly by default, but we can support streaming to Kinesis or Pub/Sub for near real-time-forwarding in dedicated/private deployments. For Hosted, we'll provide webhook pushes for critical audit events.
05:30 - Liam: SSO — Okta is our source of truth. We want SAML for login and SCIM for provisioning. Any gotchas?
05:45 - Jared: Works fine — we've done Okta SAML + SCIM in many pilots. Main items: ensure your SCIM token has user scope for groups, and map the app attributes for role provisioning. We'll send a step-by-step. There can be small timing issues with SCIM provisioning and our user caches, but it's resolvable.
06:10 - Maya: We'll set up a test Okta app and give you a test account. Jared will own the walkthrough.
06:18 - Liam: During provisioning, do we get role-based RBAC from your side or do we rely on our internal roles?
06:26 - Jared: We support role mapping via SAML assertions or SCIM group sync. You can map Okta groups to Redwood roles (admin, dev, read-only). For more granular access control we also have per-route ACLs.
07:05 - Rajiv: How do audit logs capture admin actions — who changed RBAC and when?
07:12 - Jared: Admin actions are emitted as high-fidelity audit events with actor, timestamp, IP, and the before/after diff when applicable. Those events are included in the audit log export.
08:00 - Sofia: A small thing — how do we handle service accounts for CI? We need machine-to-machine tokens without interactive SSO.
08:10 - Maya: We support API keys and short-lived tokens. For CI we recommend a service principal with SCIM-provisioned service account and fine-grained token scopes.
08:40 - Liam: On the PII front — we have endpoints that take SSNs in request bodies. Can we disable logging for that route?
08:50 - Jared: Yes — route config can set log_level = none, or redact fields via a JSON path. We'll provide examples. For the pilot please mark those routes and we'll apply the config in staging.
09:30 - Priya: Noted action: Liam to enumerate PII routes.
10:00 - Maya: On SOC2, note that our report covers the hosted product and the control environment; the Private deployment control matrix has additional controls for KMS and network isolation. We'll annotate differences.
10:32 - Liam: Are there any known gaps your security team is tracking that we should worry about?
10:40 - Jared: We've got a few low-severity items from the last internal audit; none are infra-blocking for pilots, but we'll include the remediation timeline in the summary doc.
11:05 - Rajiv: About network isolation — we plan to do VPC peering for staging, need IP ranges and NAT details.
11:15 - Maya: We'll send the IP prefixes for Redwood staging and the peering playbook. For Dedicated we can do private connectivity or direct peering; for Hosted we have an IP allowlist option.
12:00 - Sofia: Will the peering require BGP or static routes?
12:06 - Jared: Static routes are fine for the pilot; BGP is supported for larger deployments. We'll include both options.
13:00 - Liam: One outstanding compliance item — audit log retention policy. We need to map our internal policy to your retention config and confirm exports.
13:10 - Maya: We'll prepare a retention matrix: default, short-term, long-term, and export options. That will be part of the SOC2/FAQ packet.
14:50 - Rajiv: Can we get a sample audit log schema? We want to plug it into our SIEM to test parsers.
15:00 - Jared: Yes, attaching sample JSON schema in the follow-up. Note — schema may vary by runtime (Hosted vs Dedicated) but core fields are consistent: event_type, actor_id, resource, timestamp, diff.
16:30 - Sofia: On the pen-test, anything high risk?
16:40 - Maya: The pen test uncovered no high-severity vulnerabilities; a few medium/low with remediation scheduled — we'll include redacted findings.
17:10 - Liam: Any limitations around encryption keys — for example hardware-backed HSM?
17:20 - Jared: For Dedicated we support HSM-backed keys (BYOK with HSM). Hosted currently supports customer-managed KMS with envelope encryption; HSM-level is available on Private. We'll note that in the control matrix.
18:00 - Priya: Quick product note — there was a performance tuning change last week that affects batch sizing and KV cache; not security but might affect the benchmark Alicia ran. We can schedule a new benchmark after SSO is live.
18:35 - Liam: Good, once SSO is in we can run the 100-user concurrency test. What's the expected time to complete the benchmark?
18:45 - Jared: Should be 2-3 hours for a full run, plus analysis. We'll aim to do it with the staging snapshot you gave.
19:30 - Sofia: Question about deletion — if we delete a conversation under retention policy, is it hard-deleted or soft? We need legal hold support.
19:40 - Jared: We support both. Soft-delete for quick recovery, and hard-delete which purges data. For legal hold we can suspend deletion at the object level. We'll include APIs for delete and legal-hold management.
20:30 - Rajiv: Forensics — if we need to investigate an incident, can you provide raw logs and low-level traces?
20:40 - Maya: Yes — for incidents we have an escalated process to provide deeper artifacts under an NDA and a forensic package that includes trace-level logs.
21:15 - Liam: Any multi-region replication implications for data residency? Some of our customers require EU-only.
21:25 - Jared: We support region pinning for private deployments and we have EU-hosted regions for Hosted. There are replication settings you can control; for EU-only you would choose the EU region and disable cross-region failover.
22:05 - Sofia: Ok next — SCIM group sync cadence, sometimes groups lag. Is there an event for group delta?
22:12 - Jared: SCIM sends full syncs or incremental depending on the provider. Okta supports incremental group updates through SCIM v2, but there can be delays. We'll outline recommended sync cadence and conflict resolution.
23:00 - Maya: Recap: We'll share SOC2 + pen test, we will provide Okta walkthrough + test account, we'll send IP ranges and peering playbook, and Jared will share sample audit schema. Liam will send PII routes and Sofia will confirm VPC details.
23:30 - Liam: Sounds good. A couple of smaller asks: can you provide the contract language around data processing and subprocessor list?
23:45 - Maya: Yes I will put the DPA and subprocessor list in the drive.
24:00 - Priya: I'll update the POC plan in the CRM and schedule the benchmark after SSO is confirmed.
24:30 - Rajiv: One last point — encryption of logs in transit and at rest, just want confirmation TLS 1.2+ and AES256 at rest.
24:40 - Jared: Confirmed — TLS 1.2+ (we recommend TLS 1.3) and AES-256 for rest; when using customer KMS we'll leverage the configured algorithm.
25:10 - Sofia: Can you make a small note on how we revoke a user's sessions if compromised?
25:20 - Jared: Admin can revoke tokens and force re-auth; we also support immediate SCIM user disable which invalidates sessions on next check. For emergency we have token revocation API.
26:05 - Maya: Any blockers for the SSO test?
26:12 - Liam: We need the Okta test app and the steps; once we have that we'll try to provision a test user tonight.
26:25 - Jared: I'll cut the walkthrough and credentials post-call.
27:00 - Priya: For the benchmark scheduling, we'll tentatively aim for 2026-04-20 once the SSO test passes.
27:15 - Liam: Works for us.
28:00 - Rajiv: A note — we may require an SOC2 bridge letter if your report is a few months old.
28:10 - Maya: We'll check and include a bridge letter if available.
29:00 - Sofia: Are there any costs tied to audit export or KMS usage in the pilot?
29:10 - Maya: For the POC we won't bill for modest S3 exports or KMS requests; larger volumes would be discussed. We'll note these in the pilot agreement.
30:00 - Liam: Anything else on your side?
30:05 - Jared: Just that we'll provide the redaction examples and the route config snippets.
30:20 - Maya: Great. Thanks all. We'll follow up with the docs.
30:30 - Liam: Thanks.
31:00 - (ambient chatter and wrap-up)
36:00 - End of call

Notes/Artifacts to attach after call:
- SOC2_TypeII_redacted.pdf (Maya upload)
- PenTest_Summary_redacted.pdf (Maya upload)

Meeting recap / explicit next steps:

- Redwood SE: Provide Okta SAML+SCIM step-by-step and test credentials; attach sample audit log schema (Jared)
- CedarBank: Send list of PII-sensitive routes and confirm staging IP ranges (Liam & Sofia)

End transcript.
